components.name: Western Roman Empire
components.note: Romulus Augustulus deposed by Odoacer; the imperial regalia shipped to Constantinople. Incident still open.

components.name: Eastern Roman Empire
components.note: Constantinople falls to Mehmed II; Constantine XI dies in the breach. Last Roman process terminated (Trebizond, a splinter, followed in 1461).

components.name: Roman Senate
components.note: Last heard of acclaiming portraits of the emperor Phocas in 603; the Curia Julia became a church in 630. Still no quorum.

components.name: Consulship
components.note: Anicius Faustus Albinus Basilius was the last ordinary consul. Justinian quietly let the office lapse; later emperors kept the title for themselves.

components.name: Legions
components.sinceLabel: c. AD 636 (Legio V Macedonica last attested)
components.note: The last unit still carrying a legionary name disappears in Egypt during the Arab conquest. Re-enactors do not count.

components.name: Praetorian Guard
components.note: Disbanded by Constantine after the Milvian Bridge; the Castra Praetoria was demolished. Auctions of the Empire discontinued.

components.name: Aqueducts
components.note: Of the eleven ancient aqueducts, the Aqua Virgo still runs and feeds the Trevi Fountain. Roughly 1 of 11 online.

components.name: Roads
components.note: The Via Appia is still in use. Most of the ~400,000 km network is now under modern roads, fields, or your hotel.

components.name: Pantheon
components.note: Largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world; still standing, still open. A church since 609, which helped.

components.name: Colosseum
components.note: Open daily. Capacity reduced from ~50,000 spectators to timed entry. Lions: 0.

components.name: Roman concrete
components.note: Still curing. Its self-healing lime clasts were finally explained in 2023. Has outlived the organisation that poured it.

components.name: Latin
components.note: Maintenance mode at the Vatican and in law, medicine, and taxonomy. Forked into Italian, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Romanian, Catalan and friends.

components.name: Roman law
components.note: Justinian's compilation underpins civil-law systems across Europe, Latin America and beyond. Still in production.

components.name: Calendar
components.note: Forked to Gregorian in 1582. Twelve months, Roman names, Augustus still has 31 days. Julian branch maintained by several Orthodox churches.

components.name: Latin alphabet
components.note: You are reading it. Market share: most of the planet.

components.name: Roman numerals
components.note: Reduced to clock faces, film copyrights, Super Bowls and monarchs. MMXXVI and counting.

components.name: Pontifex Maximus
components.note: Held by the emperors, then by the Bishop of Rome. Still in use. Still in Rome.

components.name: Chariot racing
components.note: Last recorded races at the Circus Maximus were held by the Gothic king Totila. The Blues and Greens have been rebranded as football.

components.name: Gladiatorial games
components.note: Traditionally ended under Honorius after the death of the monk Telemachus. Replaced by reality television.
